model_annotation: The plot shows three time-series indices from 2016 to 2025, with two series referenced to the left y-axis and one series referenced to the right y-axis. The x-axis is unlabeled and uses a linear time scale with year ticks at 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024. The left y-axis is labeled “Index” and runs linearly from 0 to 1,000 with tick marks every 100; it applies to the black line “Wirtschaftspolitik insgesamt (linke Skala)” and the light-blue line “Finanzpolitik (linke Skala).” The right y-axis is also labeled “Index” and runs linearly from 0 to 9,000 with tick marks every 1,000; it applies to the mauve line “Handelspolitik (rechte Skala).” The black line is solid with no markers and fluctuates mostly around roughly 60–140 from 2016 through 2019, then rises sharply to a peak near 500 around 2020, declines through 2021 toward roughly 120–160, stays in the ~90–160 range through 2022–2024 with small spikes, and then increases steeply at the end of the series to roughly 650–700 by 2025. The light-blue line is solid with no markers and follows a similar pattern on the left scale: it varies around roughly 60–150 from 2016–2019, jumps sharply around 2020 to about 420–450, then trends downward through 2021 toward roughly 120–180, continues fluctuating mostly between about 80 and 160 through 2022–2024 with occasional spikes near ~200, and then rises sharply at the end to around 700 by 2025. The mauve line is solid with no markers and is near the bottom of the right scale for most of 2016–2019 (generally close to 0–500), shows a noticeable spike around 2019 reaching roughly 2,000, drops back near low values around 2020–2024 (mostly close to 0–200 with small fluctuations), and then surges abruptly at the end of the series to approximately 8,000–9,000 by 2025.
